SOURCE: "Rethinking Reflection in Pre-Training", Essential AI (core contributors Darsh J Shah, Peter Rushton, Somanshu Singla, Mohit Parmar, Kurt Smith, Yash Vanjani, Ashish Vaswani). arXiv:2504.04022v1 [cs.CL], 5 Apr 2025. Preprint (no venue printed).

COVERAGE: 38 of 38 pages (99,506 chars) were extracted. I read chars 0-~58,000 (body, results, conclusion), the appendices A-E, G-I opening and the end of the file, and the first part of F (F.1 math, start of F.2). I skimmed or skipped the reference list (~chars 40,000-58,000) and the middle of the appendix (F.2-F.5 dataset-pipeline details, ~chars 70,000-75,500, plus Examples 3-16 of Appendix I). The text extraction was clean. Figures are plots, so their numeric values are not in the text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Reflection appears during pre-training, before any RL or post-training. It starts early and grows with pre-training compute.
 number: OLMo-2-7B at 198B tokens already reflects. The abstract says a 7B model at 4T tokens self-corrects on all six self-reflection tasks.
 setup: OLMo-2 7B/13B/32B stage-1 pre-training checkpoints. Adversarial CoT plus the trigger "Wait,". Six tasks.
 quote: "We determine that models trained with very few training flops, like OLMo-2-7B trained with 198 billion tokens, demonstrate reflection across Mathematics, Code, Verbal, and Logical Reasoning."
 quote (abstract): "an OLMo-2-7B model pre-trained on 4 trillion tokens displays self-correction on our six self-reflection tasks."
 where: Abstract; Sec 6 (about p.12)
2. Coverage across checkpoints: most dataset-checkpoint pairs show at least one reflection instance.
 number: 231/240 pairs for situational reflection, 154/240 for self-reflection. The average Pearson r between accuracy and log(pre-training compute) is 0.76.
 setup: 40 OLMo-2 checkpoints x 6 datasets. Pre-training compute is 6nt.
 quote: "Specifically, 231 of 240 dataset-checkpoint pairs demonstrate at least one instance of situational-reflection and 154 of 240 pairs demonstrate at least one instance of self-reflection."
 quote: "leading to an average Pearson correlation between accuracy and log(pre-training compute) of 0.76 across tasks."
 where: Sec 1, p.3
3. Per-task correlations with log(compute) in the situational setting. Accuracy and explicit-reflection rate rise. Implicit accuracy is roughly flat, except on TriviaQA.
 number (Table 6; accuracy / explicit rate / implicit acc / explicit acc): BBH 0.73/0.77/0.38/0.75; cruxeval-i 0.70/0.67/0.36/0.68; cruxeval-o 0.72/0.78/-0.16/0.71; GSM8K 0.84/0.84/0.01/0.86; GSM8K-Platinum 0.84/0.85/-0.01/0.86; TriviaQA 0.72/0.49/0.62/0.70.
 setup: OLMo-2, mean of three runs. Checkpoints per task: 40 (31 for cruxeval-i).
 quote: "GSM8K-Platinum 40 0.84 0.85 -0.01 0.86"
 quote: "TriviaQA is an exception where significant improvements can be attributed to implicit reflection, a consequence of the task primarily measuring knowledge acquisition"
 where: Table 6, p.8
4. The "Wait," trigger causally raises explicit reflection and accuracy. Accuracy decomposes as a mix of two bounds: A (no trigger) and B ("Wait, I made a mistake").
 number: acc_Wait = e_Wait * acc_B + (1 - e_Wait) * i_acc_A.
 setup: GSM8K-Platinum situational, OLMo-2 checkpoints.
 quote: "its performance can be decomposed as accW ait= eW ait∗ accB + (1− eW ait) ∗ i_accA, where eW aitis the rate of explicit reflection and i_acc is the implicit reflection accuracy."
 quote: "even without a trigger, models can increasingly succeed on situational confounders as pre-training progresses."
 where: Sec 5.2, p.9; Fig 4
5. Self-reflection is harder. The self-reflection sets contain only questions every checkpoint of that size got wrong. Explicit self-reflection rate correlates strongly with compute, but accuracy correlates weakly.
 number (Table 7; accuracy r / explicit-rate r): BBH 0.44/0.88; cruxeval-i 0.69/0.70; cruxeval-o 0.38/0.49; GSM8K 0.26/0.75; GSM8K-Platinum 0.32/0.75; TriviaQA 0.09/0.73. About 64.2% of task attempts show some self-correction ability.
 quote: "Nonetheless, in about 64.2% of task attempts, the models do demonstrate at least some ability to self-correct."
 quote: "For cruxeval-i we notice that with increasing pre-training models tend to learn to self-correct. However, they are able to self-reflect much earlier."
 where: Sec 5.3, p.9-10; Table 7
6. Train-time compute trades against test-time compute. More pre-training means fewer test-time tokens for the same accuracy.
 number: train = 6nt, test = 2nw (w = words generated). Two "Wait," triggers were used.
 setup: OLMo-2-32B checkpoints, GSM8K-Platinum adversarial. The 1192B-token checkpoint was excluded as an outlier.
 quote: "as train-time compute increases, the test-time compute requirement decreases in OLMo-2-32B checkpoints."
 where: Sec 5.4, p.11; Fig 6, footnotes 5-6
7. Qwen2.5 shows the same trend with parameter count.
 number: none (Fig 7 only)
 setup: Qwen2.5 0.5B, 3B, 7B, 14B, 32B, 72B (main checkpoints). Compute varies by parameters only, because the training tokens are not given.
 quote: "with increased pre-training compute – in this case, the number of parameters – model performance on adversarial tasks consistently increases."
 where: Sec 5.5, p.11
8. Models prefer locally consistent wrong answers, and the gap narrows with pre-training.
 number: none (Fig 12)
 setup: perplexity of adversarial CoT plus correct answer minus adversarial CoT plus incorrect answer. GSM8K-Platinum, OLMo-2 7B/13B/32B.
 quote: "models consistently assign lower perplexity to incorrect answers when conditioned on misleading reasoning. This can be reflective of a local consistency bias... However, ... this perplexity gap narrows over the course of pre-training."
 where: App E, p.23-24
9. Classifier validity. Precision is high and recall is lower, so reflection is under-reported.
 number (Table 4; precision/recall/F1): cruxeval-o 0.98/0.76/0.86; GSM8K 0.95/0.71/0.81; TriviaQA 1.00/0.61/0.76.
 setup: DeepSeek-V3 prompted with 2-4 exemplars. Human gold labels: 120 questions per benchmark, 24 annotators, 360 questions, two annotators each.
 quote: "In the worst case, we will under-report reflection behaviors, but be more confident when we do report them."
 where: Sec 4.3, p.7; App G
10. Dataset sizes (Table 2; situational, then self for OLMo-2 7B/13B/32B).
 number: BBH 6511 -> 712/988/588; cruxeval-i 605 -> 276/260/181; cruxeval-o 704 -> 310/313/243; GSM8K 9070 -> 140/129/68; GSM8K-Platinum 8223 -> 113/106/50; TriviaQA 2961 -> 41/83/51.
 quote: "GSM8K 1319 9070 140, 129, 68"
 where: Table 2, p.6; App F.1
 Perturbation counts: GSM8K 1,319 x 7 = 9,233, minus 163 unchanged = 9,070. GSM8K-Platinum 1,209 x 7 = 8,463, minus 240 = 8,223.

Definitions worth keeping (Sec 3.1):
- Situational reflection: the model reflects on another source's reasoning.
- Self-reflection: the model reflects on its own output.
- Explicit reflection: tokens that recognise and address the error.
- Implicit reflection: the answer is correct with no explicit error tokens.
- Seven GSM8K perturbation types: variable initialization, arithmetic perturbation, extraneous step, step omission, each at the beginning, middle or end of the chain.
- Example: a 32B checkpoint at 4.8T tokens fixed a CruxEval input after "Wait,".

LIMITS
- The authors concede that self-reflection looks rare because the sets keep only questions all checkpoints failed ("by design, they are particularly difficult").
- How pre-trained reflection turns into post-training reasoning is left open. They hypothesise a "critical threshold of pre-trained self-reflection" but do not test it.
- They did not identify which pre-training data produces reflection ("Pinpointing data distributions ... is another natural next step").
- Pearson r is computed on log(compute) for 40 checkpoints and mixes model size with token count. The OLMo-2 checkpoints are stage-1 only (pre-anneal). Qwen2.5 varies only parameter count, and its tokens and data are unknown.
- The explicit-reflection classifier has recall of only 0.61-0.76, and it was validated on only 3 of 6 datasets.
- The adversarial CoTs come from DeepSeek-V3 and GPT-4o. Perturbations are synthetic and may not match natural errors. No RL or post-trained comparison is run, so the paper does not show that RL adds nothing.
- Training compute is only the 6nt estimate. Results are averages of three runs, with no variance reported in the text. The 1192B checkpoint was an outlier.
- The paper gives no direct pre-training objective ablation. Its point is that next-token pre-training on web data yields reflection. The authors say it is "surprising to us ... learning from organic web datasets".

BUILDS ON
- The "Wait," trigger and sequential test-time scaling are from Muennighoff et al. 2025 (budget forcing).
- It contests the claim in DeepSeek-AI 2025a (R1) that reflection "emerge[s] as a result of the model's interaction with the reinforcement learning environment".
- Models and checkpoints: OLMo et al. 2025 (OLMo-2) and Qwen et al. 2025 (Qwen2.5).
- Benchmarks: BBH (BIG-bench authors 2023), CruxEval (Gu et al. 2024), GSM8K (Cobbe et al. 2021), GSM8K-Platinum (Vendrow et al. 2025), TriviaQA (Joshi et al. 2017).
- CoT: Wei et al. 2022.
- Train/test compute trade-off: Snell et al. 2024; Kaplan et al. 2020; Hoffmann et al. 2022.
- Self-refine: Madaan et al. 2023.
- Tooling: lm-evaluation-harness (Gao et al. 2024), vLLM (Kwon et al. 2023), SGLang (Zheng et al. 2024).

CODE: Algorithms 1 and 2 are pseudocode only (p.5). The authors say code and data will be released at https://github.com/Essential-AI/reflection.
- Algorithm 1 (situational): get a correct CoT from a frontier model or dataset artifact, use F to inject small errors so the answer is wrong, append "Wait", keep the gold answer.
- Algorithm 2 (self): run checkpoint M, keep CoTs with wrong answers, append "Wait".

FIGURES (captions from the text only, not rendered)
- Fig 1, p.1: OLMo-2 checkpoints solve more adversarial GSM8K-Platinum problems as pre-training compute rises. It is the headline picture.
- Fig 2, p.2: OLMo-2-32B at 4.8T tokens on CruxEval sample_485 self-reflects after "Wait,". It is a concrete example.
- Fig 3, p.9: GSM8K-Platinum accuracy and explicit-reflection accuracy versus compute, showing explicit reflection drives the gains.
- Fig 4, p.10: no trigger (A) and "Wait, I made a mistake" (B) bound the "Wait," curve.
- Fig 5, p.10: cruxeval-i self-reflection accuracy and explicit rate.
- Fig 6, p.11: train versus test compute iso-correct lines.
- Fig 7, p.12: Qwen2.5 results.
- Fig 12, p.24: perplexity gap.
- Table 5, p.8: example reflection phrases per checkpoint, e.g. "Wait, 42.6 is not a whole number" from 7B at 38B tokens.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions. The page-1 extraction was fine. Table text is run together (Tables 1, 6 and 7 headers), so I reconstructed the columns from the order of the values. Footnote 4 says "see Table 1" for checkpoints, but they are in Appendix B. The abstract says "six self-reflection tasks", but the body says self-reflection occurred in only 154 of 240 pairs. Several numeric figure values are not recoverable from the text.

Note for the target note 06 (pretraining data and objectives): the paper does not test a specific objective or data mix. Its relevance is the claim that plain next-token pre-training on web data already produces reflective behaviour, which scales with compute.
